name: Lacto-fermentation
summary: Vegetables in a salt brine are soured by lactic bacteria; the acid and the savoury taste keep the food and add depth to a dish.
how: Weigh the vegetables and add 2 per cent salt by weight.
Press the vegetables under their own brine in a closed jar.
Keep the jar at 18 to 22 °C for 3 to 14 days and taste each day.
Chill the ferment when the acid is right, and use the juice as a sauce or a seasoning.

origin.note: Salted and soured vegetables were stored in China in the last centuries BCE; the method spread over Asia and Europe.

adoptions.via: The cooks of the Nordic kitchen, led by Noma, made ferments of vegetables, fruit and grain a part of the menu.
The plant-based menu of Eleven Madison Park used ferments in place of meat and dairy for depth of taste.
